expressions.variables.note: The id covers four skills. Re-point each old edge by what the node uses: only that a letter stands for a number (an equation or formula with a letter) -> expressions.variable.meaning; writing an expression from words -> expressions.variable.write-from-words; writing an expression for a real-world quantity -> expressions.variable.write-for-situation; substituting values into an expression -> expressions.variable.evaluate; using a formula such as A = l x w or V = s^3 in a problem -> expressions.formula.evaluate.

equations.one-step.note: x + p = q and px = q need different prerequisites for nonnegative rationals (fraction or decimal subtraction versus division), so they are two nodes. Re-point an old edge to the form it needs, or to both if it needs both. The word-problem versions are equation.one-step.addition.application and equation.one-step.multiplication.application.

coordinate-plane.four-quadrants.note: The old id joined plotting and reading, and integer and fraction or decimal coordinates. Re-point an edge to .plot when the node graphs points with integer coordinates (most 6.EE, 6.G, 7.RP and 8.F uses), to .read when it reads coordinates off a graph, and to the .fraction-decimal variants only when its points have non-integer coordinates.

decimal.division.algorithm.note: Re-point to decimal.division.by-decimal.algorithm when the divisor is a decimal (the general case; its last step uses the by-whole algorithm); re-point to decimal.division.by-whole.algorithm when only a whole-number divisor occurs, as in a unit price or mean of decimal data.

multiples.common-multiple.note: References from common-denominator steps (adding, subtracting or comparing fractions with unlike denominators) need a common multiple, not the least one: re-point them as two routes, one to factors.common-multiple.product (use b x d) and one to factors.lcm.find. A reference that only needs to recognize a common multiple goes to factors.common-multiple.meaning.

rational-numbers.operations.note: Re-point each old edge to the operation(s) the citing node's test actually uses, and to the .integers variant when its numbers are all integers, the .rationals variant when signed fractions or decimals occur. Each .rationals node depends on its .integers sibling for the sign rule.
